yearsToFirstCrop.notes: ICRAF Agroforestree Database notes only that 'trees can be grown in containers, in which case they will flower and fruit at an earlier age' (no number given).

chillUnits.notes: Evergreen subtropical/tropical tree; no source explicitly stated a chill requirement or its absence, so left null rather than assuming.

evidence.quote: The flowers provide nectar for honey bees.
evidence.doc: PROTA (Plant Resources of Tropical Africa) - Syzygium cordatum, via Pl@ntUse mirror

pollination.notes: PROTA also describes the flowers as bisexual ('Flowers bisexual, regular, usually 4-merous...') and bee-pollinated, but no source made an explicit self-fertile / needs-cross-pollinator statement, so left null rather than inferring from flower structure alone.

supplementaryReferences.title: Flowering and fruit appearance, not a ripe picking calendar
supplementaryReferences.quote: In southern Africa flowering is in August–November, and fruiting in November–March.
supplementaryReferences.doc: Brink, M. (2008), PROTA4U: Syzygium cordatum, Growth and development
supplementaryReferences.note: The original PROTA account dates flowering and fruiting but does not date ripening. SANBI describes red to dark-purple ripe berries without ripe picking months. The November–March observation is retained as southern African phenology; local food-ready picking months remain unknown.

gaps: Exact ripe picking months are not stated. The former November–March bar was withdrawn in the 11 October 2026 stage audit because the original PROTA text describes fruiting, not ripe harvest.

yearsToFirstCrop / yearsToFullBearing: searched PZA, PROTA (plantuse.plantnet.org) and ICRAF Agroforestree (speciesprofile Spid=1575, apps.worldagroforestry.org/treedb2/AFTPDFS/Syzygium_cordatum.PDF) - no numeric years-to-bearing found in any of the three; only the qualitative container-grown note above.
yieldKgPerTreeMature: no kg/tree figure found in PZA, PROTA or ICRAF Agroforestree pages for this species.
chillUnits: no source discusses chilling requirement for this evergreen indigenous species.
